sense: deserve by what one has done

evidence: Cic. Fam. 10.17.3: sī mereor, if I deserve it (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The active mereō is used in the same sense (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: a service, a kindness, that by which one deserves well of another; a merit
evidence: Cic. Fam. 1.1.1: magnitūdō tuōrum ergā mē meritōrum (Lewis & Short)
Tac. Ann. 14.53: prō ingentibus meritīs praemia accēperant (Lewis & Short)
Liv. 8.7: ignārus, laus an poena merita esset (Lewis & Short)

phrases.latin: quod, inquit, ergō, stulte, meruistī decus, minus valentem sī vīcistī fortior?
phrases.english: “Then what honour have you earned, you fool,” he said, “if you, the stronger, beat a weaker man?”
they had received rewards for their great services

phrases.latin: ignārus, laus an poena merita esset
phrases.english: not knowing whether praise or punishment was what was deserved

sources: Lewis & Short: mereo
